title: Onramp audit capsule playbook (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working PRD for a lightweight, customer-friendly audit capsule used during private (VPC / on-prem) onboarding and network handoff. The goal is to make the onboarding evidence footprint small and actionable so customers and operators can complete approvals quickly, and SRE/product teams can retain a thin, queryable audit trail that satisfies compliance reviewers.

Background / motivation:
- Private deployments generate heavy audit evidence (pcap, syslogs, full manifests) which raises storage/cost and slows onboarding reviews.
- Customers want: faster handoffs, clear proofs that changes were applied, and minimal PII in artifacts.
- Redwood needs: defensible audit artifacts for postmortem/forensics, deterministic operator UX for approvals, and a path to scale to many onboardings without exploding retention costs.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Small, canonical "audit capsule" structure for handoff evidence
- Approval gate UX (operator + automated heuristics) for onramp and network change window
- Sampling and retention strategy for capsule storage and customer copies
- CLI/SDK primitives for generating and submitting capsules during onboarding flows

Non-goals:
- Full SIEM ingestion spec (out of scope; we provide export hooks)
- Remote attestation hardware proofs (only high-level hooks here)

Success metrics (90-day, measurable):
- Median time-to-handoff reduced from current baseline by 40% for pilot customers
- Average capsule size < 150KB (compressed) for standard onramp snapshot
- Number of manual review cycles per onboarding <= 2 for 80% of pilots
- Query latency for capsule index <= 200ms for recent 90 days

Primary users / audiences:
- Customer network operators responsible for approving Redwood Private onboarding
- Redwood SRE and Solutions Engineering running handoffs and support
- Security/compliance reviewers who may request evidence for audits

User stories:
- As a customer operator, I want a short human-readable summary + signed capsule so I can approve or reject onboarding with confidence.
- As a Redwood SRE, I want minimal but sufficient evidence (connectivity checks, route table snapshot, service reachability) so I can validate slas without pulling full logs.
- As a compliance reviewer, I want an immutable capsule anchor (hash + signed receipt) stored for N years to support audits.

Proposed flow (phased onramp):
Phase A — Discovery and minimal snapshot (automated):
  - Customer runs `redwood edge-onramp init --mode=snapshot` (CLI or API).
  - CLI collects: connectivity check matrix, endpoint fingerprints, control-plane reachable boolean, customer-provided network CIDR tags, and a single signed operator statement (optional).
  - CLI produces a compressed JSON capsule (see schema below) and a capsule-hash.

Phase B — Approval gate + heuristics (operator + Redwood):
  - Operator receives capsule (email/console) with short summary and 3 toggle controls: Approve / Ask for Clarification / Reject.
  - Automated heuristics run in parallel: check for blocked IPs, service mismatch, certificate expiry within 30d. If heuristics flag high-risk, route to mandatory Solutions Eng review.
  - Approvals produce a signed approval-ticket anchored to the capsule-hash and stored in Redwood's approval ledger.

Phase C — Evidence retention & export:
  - By default, capsule is stored for 180 days in compressed form and exported once to the customer's configured S3/KMS endpoint (opt-in).
  - Sampling policy (see below) reduces retention footprint after 90 days by keeping only index records + metadata for older capsules.

Minimal audit capsule schema (human-readable explanation):
  - capsule_id: short uuid string
  - capsule_version: text (v1)
  - timestamp_utc: iso8601
  - customer_tenant_id: opaque id (no PII)
  - onramp_phase: discovery | approval | complete
  - operator_statement: short free-text (max 512 chars)
  - connectivity_matrix: list of small objects describing host:port checks (success/fail + roundtrip ms)
  - control_plane_snapshot: small key-values (api_endpoints, reachable:bool)
  - manifest_digests: list of component:sha256 (no raw configs embedded)
  - evidence_blobs: list of minimal, compressed blobs (base64) — only when necessary (default empty)
  - capsule_hash: sha256 over canonicalized payload
  - signatures: list of signatures (customer_pubkey_id or operator_id, signature_b64)
  - retention_policy: tag string (default 180d-sampled)

Notes on capsule design choices:
- Avoid storing raw credentials, raw syslogs, or PCAP inside the default capsule. If customer explicitly requests full artifacts, those are stored separately and treated as high-sensitivity with different retention.
- Use digests for manifests and build provenance to allow a later fetch if investigators need full data.
- Signatures allow customer and Redwood to rebut non-repudiation questions — we include a minimal signature envelope, not a full PKI management solution.

Approval gate heuristics (prototype rules):
- Block if any connectivity_matrix entry for control-plane is false.
- Flag if certificate expiry < 30 days.
- Flag if manifest_digests include an unvetted image hash (lookup against model registry).
- Auto-approve if all control-plane checks pass and operator_statement == "auto-approve" and customer tier == self-serve pilot.

Sampling & retention model (cost-aware):
- Retention tiers: 0-30d (hot, full capsule, searchable), 31-180d (warm, index + metadata + 1 compressed blob), >180d (cold, index entry + anchored hash only).
- Sampling budget: for large customers we keep every capsule for 90d then sample 1-in-N (configurable) for long-term retention, N determined by contractual SLAs.
- Index design: single-row per capsule keyed by capsule_hash, timestamp, customer_tenant_id, minimal tags. Index must be queryable by time range and tenant quickly.

CLI/SDK primitives (proposal):
- redwood edge-onramp init --collect=connectivity,manifests --operator="name" --customer-id=123
- redwood edge-onramp sign --key-id=operator-1 capsule.json -> capsule.signed.json
- API: POST /private/v1/capsules -> returns capsule_id and capsule_hash
- Webhook: on approval, Redwood will call customer-specified webhook with approval ticket and capsule_hash

UX sample (console digest):
- Short headline: "Onramp snapshot for tenant: acme-corp — control-plane reachable: YES — checks: 12/12 passed"
- Expandable details: show connectivity_matrix rows, manifest summary, operator statement, download signed capsule link

Rollout plan (6-12 weeks pilot):
- Weeks 1–2: implement capsule generator + canonicalizer + minimal signing in CLI; unit tests + examples
- Weeks 3–4: integrate approval gate UI + webhook; SRE dogfood with 2 pilot customers
- Weeks 5–6: implement retention sampling and export rules; monitoring/alerts for failed heuristics
- Weeks 7–8: iterate on heuristics, add opt-in full artifact upload flow, finalize docs and runbook

Open questions / risks:
- Do customers want the default export to their storage or to keep it with Redwood? (privacy/ops tradeoff)
- How to manage key lifecycle for operator signatures long-term (rotation, revocation)?
- Can we safely rely on small digests only for forensic needs, or will compliance teams require full artifacts faster than we anticipate?
- Legal/retention differences across jurisdictions — need compliance sign-off for per-country defaults.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Align with Legal on retention defaults and export consent language (owner: Maya) [due 2024-11-25]
- Spike: implement proto-capsule generator in CLI (owner: Ethan) [due 2024-10-04]
- Run two pilot onramps with Solutions Eng (customers: pilot-acme, pilot-borealis) and collect feedback (owner: Lina) [start 2024-10-14]

Appendix — example compact capsule (v1) (plain JSON, illustrative; not nested beyond text):
{
  "capsule_id": "c7f9a3e2-xxxx-xxxx",
  "timestamp_utc": "2024-10-01T21:12:03Z",
  "customer_tenant_id": "tenant-0021",
  "onramp_phase": "discovery",
  "operator_statement": "initial snapshot before handoff",
  "connectivity_matrix": ["api.redwood.internal:443:ok:32ms","10.0.0.1:22:ok:14ms"],
  "control_plane_snapshot": "api_endpoints=2;reachable=true",
  "manifest_digests": ["bootstrap:v1:sha256:aa11bb"],
  "evidence_blobs": [],
  "capsule_hash": "sha256:3ab2...",
  "signatures": ["operator:JunPark:MEUCIQ..."],
  "retention_policy": "180d-sampled"
}

Rationale for uniqueness of this doc:
- Focused on a tiny, UX-first capsule for onboarding (not operator ledger internals or full attestation).
- Explicit CLI and console UX primitives to make the handoff friction minimal.
- Sampling-forward retention model that balances cost and auditability.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please comment inline in the Confluence page linked in linked_artifacts. I'm intentionally keeping the capsule small — if your team expects richer telemetry, list exact fields we'd need to promote into v2.

-- Maya
